lesson_title: Tell the Term in Six Minutes
hook_text: Problem, findings, two ideas, the drawing, the model, the price, why you. Six minutes, everyone speaks, no bluffing.
clip_script: The board has to spend the school's money, so they listen for four things: do you get the problem, does the design meet the specs, is the price real, can you be trusted to build it. Evidence, not claims: not very safe but 1 in 12, landings of 1 200, rails at 900, here on the plan. Tell it in IDMEC order: half a minute opening, a minute on what you found, two on the brief, the two ideas, the scorecard and the drawing, one on the model, one on the budget, a close with three reasons. One stage each. Rehearse with a timer. Questions: point to the number. Do not know? Say so. Then sit on the board and score the other bids on the sheet, with reasons, not by friendship.
visual_style: Whiteboard boardroom sketch; a six-segment timer bar labelled with the IDMEC stages; a hand pointing at a model; a scoring sheet filling with numbers and reasons.
mood: Composed, a little nervous energy turned into order.
pacing: Four things, evidence, the six parts, questions, scoring.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and time a one-minute summary of your own project.
